name: agent_session_containment

storage.rationale: The safeguard writes one systemd user slice unit inside the invoking user's home and starts it; it needs no privilege and creates no host-wide state.

description: Write and verify vrooli-agents.slice under the invoking user's systemd manager so every coding-agent session is born inside a CPU, memory and task ceiling that a build storm cannot escape

cpu_weight.description: systemd CPUWeight= of the agent slice. 100 is a neutral share; 50 gives the supervisors (400) eight times the share under contention.

memory_high_percent.description: MemoryHigh= as a percentage of physical memory: the slice is throttled above it.

memory_max_percent.description: MemoryMax= as a percentage of physical memory: the kernel reclaims and kills inside the slice above it, before the host swaps. Must not be below memory_high_percent.

tasks_max.description: TasksMax= of the slice: the most threads and processes every agent session together may hold. A fork storm stops here.

linux.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

macos.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

windows.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

macos.evidence: No slice on macOS; the launcher applies the same ceilings per session through the rlimit-exec shim (RLIMIT_NPROC from tasks_max, RLIMIT_AS from memory_max_percent). Verified by platform-go fixtures, not on a macOS host.

windows.evidence: No slice on Windows; the launcher assigns each session to a Job Object with a memory, active-process and CPU-rate quota. Verified by platform-go fixtures, not on a Windows host.
